summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging after merging the release PR, then investigate and fix performance/auth issues discovered during smoke testing.
summary.outcome: v0.25.1 was released (including a Dockerfile fix) and deployed to staging. Root causes for slow IPNS publish and broken token refresh were identified, with IPNS fix merged (PR #308) and a broader API client consolidation refactor initiated.

repo: The staging deploy workflow triggers on `v*-staging*` tags, not release tags — staging deployment is intentionally manual via the 'Tag Staging Release' GitHub Actions workflow.

release-please `pull-request-title-pattern` must include `${component}` in multi-package repos, otherwise it cannot match merged PRs back to components and aborts with 'untagged, merged release PRs outstanding'.

The API is a zero-knowledge server that never handles plaintext — it stores opaque blobs and proxies IPFS, so it genuinely has no workspace package dependencies. The `api-client` package is generated from the OpenAPI spec and acts as the typed bridge.

The `packages/crypto` COPY in `apps/api/Dockerfile` was stale — the API does not depend on any `@cipherbox/*` workspace packages, and the stale COPY was pulling in `@cipherbox/core` transitively via the lockfile.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances hibernate after inactivity and return HTTP 503 on wake — Grafana provisioning step failures are likely transient.

There are three separate HTTP client paths in the web app: (1) orval react-query fetch mutator `custom-instance.ts`, (2) hand-written axios client `lib/api/client.ts` for auth/vault init, (3) hand-written `lib/api/ipfs.ts`. Token refresh interceptor only existed on path 2.

The web app has its own orval config generating 8,812 lines of react-query hooks, but almost none of the hooks are used — the app imports raw generated functions everywhere. Only `useHealthControllerCheck` is used as a hook (2 locations).

The `@cipherbox/api-client` package uses `axios-functions` orval mode for framework-agnostic consumers (SDK, desktop). The web app's duplicate orval config uses `react-query` mode but the react-query hooks are largely unused.

IPNS `publishRecord()` was awaiting the delegated routing DHT publish via the `someguy` sidecar. DHT propagation takes 10-30s inherently, but `resolveRecord()` always prefers the DB cache, making the await unnecessary.

code.finding: Stale COPY of `packages/crypto/package.json` caused `pnpm deploy` to fail when the lockfile required `@cipherbox/core` (a devDep of crypto). Removed since API has no workspace deps.
`pull-request-title-pattern` was `'chore: release'` without `${component}`, breaking release-please in multi-package mode — it could not match merged PRs to components.
`result` variable stays `'success'` after fire-and-forget refactor — correct because the DB record save is the authoritative publish; DHT propagation is best-effort.
Orval-generated fetch mutator for react-query hooks — had zero 401 handling, causing unrecoverable auth failures on sessions longer than the 15-minute access token lifetime.
Separate web-app orval config generating react-query wrappers from the same OpenAPI spec as `packages/api-client`. Identified as redundant — targeted for deletion in consolidation refactor.
Uses `client: 'axios-functions'` mode — generates framework-agnostic functions. Auth injected via `setApiClientConfig({ getAccessToken })`. No built-in 401 refresh — delegates to consumer.

workflow: When release-please is stuck on 'untagged, merged release PRs', manually creating the git tag and GitHub release from the correct commit unblocks it without needing to revert or re-run anything.
`chore` commits do not trigger release-please version bumps — use `fix` for broken CI/build issues to get a patch release.
The Tag Staging Release workflow runs E2E tests and waits for staging-approval before creating the staging tag, so the release tag must include all fixes before triggering it.
Spawning parallel debugger agents for independent issues (IPNS perf + token refresh) is effective — both investigations ran concurrently and returned root causes.

friction: release-please silently aborted tag creation after PR #306 merged — the only indication was a cryptic 'untagged, merged release PRs outstanding' log buried in the Actions output.

The missing `${component}` in `pull-request-title-pattern` was a latent misconfiguration introduced when migrating to multi-package release-please — it only surfaced when a second release was attempted.
Three separate HTTP client paths in the web app made it unclear where to add token refresh logic, and the orval fetch mutator having no auth handling was a non-obvious gap.

Stale Dockerfile COPY (`packages/crypto`) caused a build failure that wasn't caught until the first staging deployment attempt post-release — no local Docker build validation in CI for the API image before tagging.
open_items: Consolidation of web app HTTP clients: delete `apps/web/src/api/` (orval react-query generation), `apps/web/orval.config.ts`, and `apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts`; migrate all imports to `@cipherbox/api-client` with 401/refresh interceptor added to the package. Refactor agent was spawned but work is in-progress.
Token refresh fix (PR from debugger agent) was stashed/superseded by the api-client consolidation refactor — needs to land as part of that refactor, not as a standalone fix.
Add `withCredentials: true` to `@cipherbox/api-client` axios instance (needed for HTTP-only refresh token cookies) as part of the consolidation.
Consider adding local Docker build validation to CI for `apps/api` to catch missing workspace package COPYs before they reach staging.
Grafana provisioning step in the staging deploy is fragile on free-tier (hibernation/503) — consider adding a retry or a pre-warm step.
